recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It fixes remaining current-build syntax drift from FHIR-3860 and aligns the HTTP page with later no-filter search guidance without changing search semantics or adding redundant prose.
issue_request: FHIR-3860 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for DSTU1. It requested REST search syntax that makes the query string and search parameters optional, approving optional-brace syntax such as GET [base]/[type]{?[parameters]{&_format=[mime-type]}} and noting application in svn 4594.
initial_application: Git-svn commit 9b37f384b7c53ea94e4e7152f111269458d338d2 (#3860 / svn 4594) applied the issue to source/http.html for type, POST, and compartment search patterns, but the all-resource pattern remained required-looking. Later commit 7415a1eb0824ba59d977db335205d71eed004312, for FHIR-35859/FHIR-37822, refactored HTTP search examples and left multi-type and all-type examples with required-looking [parameters] syntax.
additional_context: FHIR-19523 later added current source/search.html conformance text stating that no-filter searches such as GET [base], GET [base]/Patient, POST [base]/_search, and POST [base]/Patient/_search with no body should return all records in scope unless rejected as overly broad. Exact FHIR-3860 Zulip and Confluence searches found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: Updated source/http.html to mark additional multi-type filters optional, to use optional-brace syntax for all-resource GET and POST search, and to remove the malformed POST _search '?{?' query syntax. source/search.html was left unchanged because it already carries the no-filter conformance rule.
source_changes: source/http.html:1639-1653 changed multi-type and all-resource search syntax examples so additional search parameters are optional and POST _search no longer includes malformed '?{?' syntax.

related_jiras.note: Later Published issue explicitly states that no search parameters returns all records in scope, confirming the need for optional search-parameter syntax.
Later HTTP-page POST-search work introduced the current syntax block that needed reconciliation, but the issue itself was not separately decided here.
